messages.text: In the harlo os for NerdQaxe ++ v5 and v6 compatible with adding a Ethernet connector to the solo mining rig?
I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check the current Harlo OS notes before I answer.
Searched the web · NerdQaxe++ ethernet support ESP32-S3 W5500

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist.

Short answer: I will not guess on this one, so here is what I can confirm and what I am getting checked.

What is true at the hardware level: the NerdQaxe++ is ESP32-S3 based and has no Ethernet port of its own. Wired networking is done with a W5500 SPI adapter (a "HAT" / interposer) on the display header, and 
upstream ESP-Miner for the NerdQAxe family added W5500 support for the NerdQAxe+, NerdQAxe++ and NerdOCTAXE-Gamma, with the firmware probing the W5500 at boot so the same binary works with or without the HAT; it was tested on real NerdQAxe++ hardware, where link and DHCP come up and it mines over Ethernet
. 
The community-standard pinout for that adapter is MOSI=12, MISO=16, SCLK=2, CS=21, and the miner prefers the wired link and falls back to WiFi automatically
.

What I cannot confirm: whether Harlo OS v5 and v6 specifically carry that W5500 board support for the NerdQaxe++. Harlo OS is our own build, not the upstream binary, so the upstream result does not automatically apply. I have asked JD, our hardware lead, to confirm which Harlo OS release enables Ethernet on the NerdQaxe++ and with which adapter.

Faster route if you want it now: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , ask in the Harlo OS channel and tag @nullhashrate (JD). He and the community are very active there.

One thing that helps me: is this for a unit you already run (and if so, which Harlo OS version does its web UI show), or are you planning the build before you buy?
Handed to the team · Cannot confirm from Harlo OS docs whether W5500 Ethernet board support is built
The team has this and JD will come back on it, usually within one business day. If you stay in the chat he can jump in directly; if you step away you will get the answer by email.
I already own a NerdQaxe  v5 and a NerdQaxe v6 and I am planning to add the Ethernet adapter as you explain. Would like to consider flashing the harlo os if it works wit Ethernet
Good, that helps. Let me see whether the Harlo OS flasher lists the NerdQaxe++ board revisions and anything about wired networking.
Searched the web · Harlo OS firmware supported devices NerdQaxe++ release notes

Thanks, that narrows it nicely. Here is what I can confirm now, with sources.

1. Board support: Harlo OS runs on the NerdQaxe++ family. Our own compatibility page lists 
the NerdQaxe++ Rev 6.1 as running it today
, and the Harlo OS announcement lists 
the BSB NerdQaxe++ among the supported models, plus NerdQaxe++ Rev7
. So a Rev 5.x and a Rev 6.1 board are both in the family JD builds for. The flasher at harlolabs.com shows the exact model list, so pick the one that matches each board before you install.

2. Ethernet in Harlo OS: the feature list for the OS includes 
Stratum V2 and three saved networks with Ethernet always winning
, so wired is a first-class path in the network manager, not an afterthought. What I still will not state as fact is whether the current Harlo OS build probes and drives a W5500 SPI adapter on the NerdQaxe++ display header the way upstream does. That is exactly the question JD has from me.

3. For reference, on the upstream side the adapter is a W5500 interposer on the display header using 
SCLK 2, MOSI 12, MISO 16, CS 21, with the firmware preferring the wired link and falling back to WiFi automatically
, and 
it is detected at boot by reading the W5500 version register, so the same binary works with or without the HAT fitted
. One warning worth noting before you buy the adapter: 
on boards where a CAN extension shares GPIO21 and GPIO16, do not fit the LAN adapter and the CAN board at the same time
.

Two things that will make JD's answer precise, if you can post them:

1. The exact board revision printed on each PCB (for example Rev 5.1 and Rev 6.1).
2. Which W5500 adapter you plan to buy (a Jabitaxe style LAN kit, a generic breakout, or a ready made HAT).

Fastest route while you wait: our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , drop the two answers above in the Harlo OS channel and tag @nullhashrate (JD). He is on most days and can tell you straight away which build to flash.

One safety note on flashing: the factory image erases saved settings and WiFi credentials, so note your pool URL, worker name and any overclock values first. If a unit is under warranty from another seller, flashing different firmware can affect that with them.
Jabitaxe LAN Adapter Kit for NerdQaxe++ and NerdOCTAXE

Good, that is the one with the most community history, so this is the best case.

What that means technically: the Jabitaxe kit is the adapter the NerdQaxe LAN forks are built around. It sits on the T-Display S3 header and runs the W5500 on a dedicated SPI2 bus at MOSI 12, MISO 16, SCLK 2, CS 21, RST 13, INT 11, the miner prefers the wired link and falls back to WiFi on its own, and DNS is applied over the Ethernet interface so stratum resolves correctly. That is the same pinout upstream used when it added W5500 support to the NerdQAxe+, NerdQAxe++ and NerdOCTAXE-Gamma, and that work was tested on real NerdQAxe++ hardware with link and DHCP coming up and the board mining over Ethernet. So the kit itself is the right choice for both your units.

The one open piece is still whether the Harlo OS build you would flash carries that same W5500 detection for the NerdQaxe++. JD has that question from me.

Last thing I need from you: the board revision printed on each PCB, for example Rev 5.1 and Rev 6.1. It matters because on the NerdOCTAXE-Gamma rev3.4 those SPI pins are shared with the TMP451 temperature mux, so the HAT is not usable there, and revision is how we rule that kind of clash out on your two boards. A photo of each board near the silkscreen works if the text is small.

Meanwhile, ask in the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and tag @nullhashrate (JD), saying you have the Jabitaxe kit and want to know the Harlo OS build for a NerdQaxe++. He answers there most days.
